source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־בְּגָדָ֑יו וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק וַיָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as heard the king Hezekiah, and he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went [into the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And it was, when King Hezekiah heard [it], [that] he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went [into] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: As soon as King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, wrapped himself in sackcloth, and entered the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: King Hezekiah heard the report of what the Assyrian commander had said. He tore his clothes and put on rough sackcloth to show his grief. Then he went into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the story continues from 36:22 and runs parallel to 2 Kings 19:1-37
decisions.reason: Chapters 36-39 closely match 2 Kings 18:13-20:19. What Hezekiah heard is the report his officials brought back from the Rabshakeh (36:22).

decisions.choice: tearing clothes and wearing sackcloth: signs of grief and of humbling oneself before God
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was a rough cloth of goat or camel hair worn in mourning and repentance (22:12; Jonah 3:6). The king goes at once to the house of the LORD to seek help.

decisions.choice: the report of what the Assyrian commander had said; to show his grief
decisions.reason: Readable says what Hezekiah heard (36:22) and what the gestures meant.

source.text: וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת־אֶלְיָקִ֨ים אֲשֶׁר־עַל־הַבַּ֜יִת וְאֵ֣ת׀שֶׁבְנָ֣א הַסּוֹפֵ֗ר וְאֵת֙ זִקְנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים אֶל־יְשַֽׁעְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־אָמ֖וֹץ הַנָּבִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent Eliakim who [was] over the house and Shebna the secretary and [the] elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet.

en.L: And he sent Eliakim, who [was] over the house, and Shebna the secretary, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet.
en.B: He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests, all clothed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
en.R: He sent Eliakim, the man in charge of the palace, Shebna the royal secretary, and the leading priests to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. They were all wearing sackcloth.

decisions.choice: over the house: the chief steward of the palace; the secretary: the royal scribe
decisions.reason: These are the same officials who met the Rabshakeh (36:3). Eliakim had been given Shebna's post as steward (22:15-22); Shebna now serves as the king's secretary, who wrote and kept the royal records.

decisions.choice: the elders of the priests: the senior priests
decisions.reason: The phrase means the leading or older priests, not a separate council (2 Kings 19:2; Jeremiah 19:1).

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ יוֹם־צָרָ֧ה וְתוֹכֵחָ֛ה וּנְאָצָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י בָ֤אוּ בָנִים֙ עַד־מַשְׁבֵּ֔ר וְכֹ֥חַ אַ֖יִן לְלֵדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Thus says Hezekiah: a day of distress and rebuke and disgrace [is] the day this, for have come children to [the] opening [of the womb] and strength there is not to give birth.

en.L: And they said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: A day of distress and rebuke and disgrace [is] this day, for children have come to the opening [of the womb], and [there is] no strength to give birth.
en.B: They said to him, "Hezekiah says this: Today is a day of distress, of rebuke and of disgrace. Children have reached the opening of the womb, and there is no strength to bring them to birth.
en.R: They said to Isaiah, "This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of trouble. We are being punished and put to shame. We are like a woman whose baby is ready to be born, but she has no strength left to give birth.

decisions.choice: rebuke: correction or punishment that brings shame
decisions.reason: The word is used for God's stern correction (Hosea 5:9). Here it may also include the enemy's insults, which the next word, disgrace, picks up.

decisions.choice: children have come to the opening of the womb: a crisis at its decisive moment with no power to finish it
decisions.reason: A birth that has come to the last stage but cannot be completed means danger of death for mother and child (Hosea 13:13). Judah is at the point of crisis and helpless to come through it.

decisions.choice: We are like a woman whose baby is ready to be born
decisions.reason: Readable turns the image into a stated comparison so the reader sees what it describes.

source.text: אוּלַ֡י יִשְׁמַע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֵ֣ת׀דִּבְרֵ֣י רַב־שָׁקֵ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שְׁלָח֨וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֤וּר׀אֲדֹנָיו֙ לְחָרֵף֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַ֔י וְהוֹכִ֨יחַ֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖ע יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְנָשָׂ֣אתָ תְפִלָּ֔ה בְּעַ֥ד הַשְּׁאֵרִ֖ית הַנִּמְצָאָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Perhaps will hear Yahweh your God the words of [the] Rabshakeh whom has sent him the king of Assyria his master to taunt [the] God living, and he will rebuke [him for] the words that has heard Yahweh your God; and you will lift up prayer for the remnant that is found.

en.L: Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria, his master, has sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke [him for] the words that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has heard. And lift up a prayer for the remnant that is found."
en.B: Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will hear what the chief officer said when his master the king of Assyria sent him to insult the living God, and will call him to account for the words {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has heard. Lift up a prayer, then, for the remnant that is still here."
en.R: Maybe {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will pay attention to what the Assyrian commander said. His master, the king of Assyria, sent him to insult the living God. Maybe {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will punish him for what he said. So please pray for those of us who are still left."

decisions.choice: the living God: the God who acts, unlike the lifeless gods of the nations
decisions.reason: To insult the living God is to treat him like the idols Assyria has burned (verse 19; 1 Samuel 17:26). The phrase returns in Hezekiah's prayer (verse 17).

decisions.choice: the remnant that is found: those still left in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Assyria had already taken the fortified towns of Judah (36:1). Only Jerusalem and the people in it remained.

decisions.choice: the Rabshakeh (L); the chief officer (B); the Assyrian commander (R)
decisions.reason: An Assyrian title (see 36:2). Literal keeps the title; Balanced and Readable give its sense.

decisions.choice: call him to account
decisions.reason: The verb means to rebuke or punish; Balanced uses a phrase that covers both.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַבְדֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶל־יְשַׁעְיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came the servants of the king Hezekiah to Isaiah.

en.L: And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
en.B: So King Hezekiah's officials came to Isaiah.
en.R: So King Hezekiah's officials went to Isaiah.

decisions.choice: they came: a summary of the visit already told in verses 2-4
decisions.reason: The narrator returns to the action after giving the officials' message, and verse 6 gives Isaiah's answer.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his court officials, as elsewhere in Isaiah.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן אֶל־אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֑ם כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־תִּירָא֙ מִפְּנֵ֤י הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר גִּדְּפ֛וּ נַעֲרֵ֥י מֶלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֖וּר אוֹתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Isaiah, Thus you will say to your master: thus says Yahweh, Do not be afraid of the words that you have heard, which have blasphemed the young men of the king of Assyria me.

en.L: And Isaiah said to them, "Thus you will say to your master: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Do not be afraid because of the words that you have heard, with which the young men of the king of Assyria have blasphemed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Isaiah said to them, "Say to your master, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Do not be frightened by what you have heard, the words with which the king of Assyria's lackeys have reviled {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Do not be afraid of the words you heard. The king of Assyria's men have insulted {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: the young men: a scornful word for the Assyrian envoys
decisions.reason: The word means boys or attendants. God does not call them servants or officials, as Hezekiah's men are called (verse 5), but treats them as mere underlings.

decisions.choice: blasphemed: insulted God with words
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in verse 23. The envoys' speech (36:18-20) put the LORD on a level with the gods that had failed.

decisions.choice: lackeys
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the scorn of the word; Literal keeps its plain sense.

source.text: הִנְנִ֨י נוֹתֵ֥ן בּוֹ֙ ר֔וּחַ וְשָׁמַ֥ע שְׁמוּעָ֖ה וְשָׁ֣ב אֶל־אַרְצ֑וֹ וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Here I [am] putting in him a spirit, and he will hear a report and he will return to his land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his land.

en.L: Look, I am putting a spirit in him, and he will hear a report and return to his land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his land.'"
en.B: I am about to put a spirit in him: he will hear a rumor and go back to his own country, and in his own country I will make him fall by the sword.'"
en.R: Listen! I will make him want to leave. He will hear a report and go back to his own country. And there in his own country I will have him killed with a sword.'"

decisions.choice: a spirit: an impulse or frame of mind that God puts in him
decisions.reason: God moves the king's will from within (19:14; 1 Kings 22:22). It need not be fear, but it makes him turn for home.

decisions.choice: the report and the sword: both come true later in the chapter
decisions.reason: He hears news about Tirhakah (verse 9), returns home (verse 37), and dies by the sword in his own land (verse 38).

decisions.choice: I will make him want to leave
decisions.reason: Readable states what the spirit does in this story.

source.text: וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ רַב־שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּמְצָא֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר נִלְחָ֖ם עַל־לִבְנָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י נָסַ֖ע מִלָּכִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned [the] Rabshakeh and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had set out from Lachish.

en.L: And the Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had set out from Lachish.
en.B: The chief officer went back and found the king of Assyria attacking Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
en.R: The Assyrian commander went back to the king of Assyria. He had heard that the king had left the town of Lachish. He found him fighting against the town of Libnah.

decisions.choice: Lachish and Libnah: fortified towns in the low hills southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Sennacherib had been besieging Lachish (36:2). His palace carvings at Nineveh show the siege and capture of Lachish. Libnah lay a few miles to the north of it.

decisions.choice: he had heard: the Rabshakeh; he had set out: the king
decisions.reason: The Rabshakeh went back to Lachish, learned the king had moved on, and found him at Libnah.

decisions.choice: the Rabshakeh (L); the chief officer (B); the Assyrian commander (R)
decisions.reason: An Assyrian title (see 36:2). Literal keeps the title; Balanced and Readable give its sense.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע עַל־תִּרְהָ֤קָה מֶֽלֶךְ־כּוּשׁ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יָצָ֖א לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם אִתָּ֑ךְ וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, saying, He has come out to fight with you. And he heard and he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

en.L: And he heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, "He has come out to fight with you." And he heard [it], and he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
en.B: Then the king heard that Tirhakah king of Cush was marching out to fight against him. When he heard this, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
en.R: Then the king of Assyria received news about Tirhakah, the king of Cush, the land south of Egypt. Tirhakah was coming out to fight against him. When the king of Assyria heard this, he sent messengers to Hezekiah. He told them,

decisions.choice: Tirhakah king of Cush: a ruler of the Cushite kings who governed Egypt
decisions.reason: Cush lay south of Egypt on the Nile. Its kings ruled Egypt in this period. Tirhakah became king about 690 BC; in 701 BC he may have led the army as a prince, and the account gives him the title he later held.

decisions.choice: he heard and he sent: a second message, after the Rabshakeh's speech in chapter 36
decisions.reason: The parallel 2 Kings 19:9 reads "he again sent". Both accounts describe the same second embassy, now with a letter (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the land south of Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable explains where Cush was.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־יַשִּֽׁאֲךָ֣ אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בּוֹטֵ֥חַ בּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus you will say to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying: Let not deceive you your God in whom you [are] trusting, saying, Not will be given Jerusalem into [the] hand of [the] king of Assyria.

en.L: "Thus you will speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying: 'Do not let your God, in whom you are trusting, deceive you, saying, "Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."
en.B: "Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: 'Do not let your God, the one you rely on, deceive you by saying, "Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria."
en.R: "Tell King Hezekiah of Judah this: 'You trust in your God. He tells you that Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria. Do not let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} fool you.

decisions.choice: deceive you: Sennacherib now calls God himself a deceiver
decisions.reason: In 36:14-15 he warned against trusting Hezekiah; now he says the LORD's own promise is a lie. This is the insult Hezekiah lays before God (verses 14-17).

decisions.choice: saying: the promise is what God says
decisions.reason: The words about Jerusalem are presented as God's promise, given through Isaiah and repeated by Hezekiah (36:15).

source.text: הִנֵּ֣ה׀אַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֜וּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר לְכָל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת לְהַחֲרִימָ֑ם וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּנָּצֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, you have heard what have done the kings of Assyria to all the lands, by devoting them to destruction; and you, will you be delivered?

en.L: Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction, and you will be delivered?
en.B: You yourself have heard how the kings of Assyria dealt with all the lands, wiping them out. And you expect to escape?
en.R: You have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to every other country. They destroyed them completely. Do you think you will be saved?

decisions.choice: devoting them to destruction: destroying them completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for putting a people under a ban of total destruction (Deuteronomy 7:2). Here it simply means utter destruction.

decisions.choice: and you will be delivered?: a scornful question expecting no
decisions.reason: The question has no question word; the tone makes it a taunt: you alone will escape?

source.text: הַהִצִּ֨ילוּ אוֹתָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִשְׁחִ֣יתוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֶת־גּוֹזָ֖ן וְאֶת־חָרָ֑ן וְרֶ֥צֶף וּבְנֵי־עֶ֖דֶן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּתְלַשָּֽׂר׃

records.literal_gloss: Did deliver them the gods of the nations whom destroyed my fathers, Gozan and Haran and Rezeph and [the] sons of Eden who [were] in Telassar?

en.L: Did the gods of the nations deliver them, which my fathers destroyed, Gozan and Haran and Rezeph and the sons of Eden who [were] in Telassar?
en.B: Did the gods of the nations my forefathers destroyed rescue them, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
en.R: The kings before me destroyed the nations of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, and the people of Eden who lived in Telassar. Did the gods of those nations save them?

decisions.choice: my fathers: the kings before me
decisions.reason: The word means ancestors, and here the earlier kings of Assyria, whether or not they were the speaker's own forebears.

decisions.choice: Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, Eden, Telassar: towns and lands in upper Mesopotamia conquered by Assyria
decisions.reason: Gozan lay on the Habor River (2 Kings 17:6) and Haran on the Balikh (Genesis 11:31). Eden is the land Assyrian records call Bit-Adini, on the upper Euphrates.

source.text: אַיֵּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־חֲמָת֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַרְפָּ֔ד וּמֶ֖לֶךְ לָעִ֣יר סְפַרְוָ֑יִם הֵנַ֖ע וְעִוָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Where [is the] king of Hamath and [the] king of Arpad and [the] king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?

en.L: Where [is] the king of Hamath and the king of Arpad and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?'"
en.B: Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, or of Ivvah?'"
en.R: Where is the king of Hamath now? Where are the kings of Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?'"

decisions.choice: Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim: cities in Syria and beyond that Assyria had taken
decisions.reason: Hamath and Arpad were named in the Rabshakeh's speech (36:19; see also 10:9). People from Sepharvaim and Ivvah were resettled in Samaria after its fall (2 Kings 17:24).

decisions.choice: of the city of: introduces Sepharvaim
decisions.reason: The word is read as "of the city". Some take it as the name of another town, Lair.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ אֶת־הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֨עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Hezekiah the letters from [the] hand of the messengers and he read it, and he went up [to the] house of Yahweh and spread it out Hezekiah before Yahweh.

en.L: And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read it, and he went up [to] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and Hezekiah spread it out before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it through. He went up to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and opened it out in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The messengers handed Hezekiah the letter, and he read it. Then he went up to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. There he opened the letter out flat in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the letters ... read it: one letter, written as a plural
decisions.reason: The noun is plural, but the pronouns are singular, so it is one document, perhaps of several sheets. The parallel 2 Kings 19:14 reads "read them".

decisions.choice: spread it out before the LORD: laid the letter open in the temple as a plea
decisions.reason: Hezekiah puts the insults before God himself, as if presenting evidence to a judge, and then prays (verse 15).

decisions.choice: the letter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the singular, matching the pronouns; Literal keeps the plural noun.

source.text: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And prayed Hezekiah to Yahweh, saying,

en.L: And Hezekiah prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying,
en.B: Then Hezekiah prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.R: Then Hezekiah prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said,

decisions.choice: he prayed: the prayer of verses 16-20
decisions.reason: The parallel 2 Kings 19:15 reads "prayed before the LORD". The prayer praises God, asks him to listen, states the danger, and asks for rescue so that the world may know him.

source.text: יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אַתָּה־ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh of hosts, God of Israel, sitting [on] the cherubim, you he [is] the God, you alone, of all [the] kingdoms of the earth; you made the heavens and the earth.

en.L: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, God of Israel, who sits [on] the cherubim, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, the God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made the heavens and the earth.
en.B: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and no one else, are God of every kingdom on earth. It was {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who made the heavens and the earth.
en.R: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sit as king above the cherubim, the winged creatures over the ark of the covenant. You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.

decisions.choice: who sits on the cherubim: enthroned above the winged figures over the ark
decisions.reason: Two golden cherubim spread their wings over the ark in the most holy place, and God was pictured as seated above them as king (Exodus 25:18-22; 1 Samuel 4:4; Psalm 99:1). The verb can mean to sit or to be enthroned.

decisions.choice: you alone are God: the LORD is the only God and the Maker of all things
decisions.reason: Against Sennacherib's claim that no god could resist him (verses 10-13), Hezekiah confesses that the LORD alone is God over every kingdom, because he made heaven and earth (44:24; 45:5-7). The parallel 2 Kings 19:15 lacks "of hosts".

decisions.choice: the winged creatures over the ark of the covenant
decisions.reason: Readable explains the cherubim.

source.text: הַטֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה׀אָזְנְךָ֙ וּֽשְׁמָ֔ע פְּקַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה עֵינֶ֖ךָ וּרְאֵ֑ה וּשְׁמַ֗ע אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י סַנְחֵרִ֔יב אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֔ח לְחָרֵ֖ף אֱלֹהִ֥ים חָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Incline, Yahweh, your ear and hear; open, Yahweh, your eyes and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib that he has sent to taunt [the] God living.

en.L: Incline, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear and hear; open, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to taunt the living God.
en.B: Turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and listen; open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and look. Hear every word Sennacherib has sent to insult the living God.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please listen and hear. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, open {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes and see. Listen to everything Sennacherib has said. He sent his message to insult the living God.

decisions.choice: incline your ear, open your eyes: asking God to take notice and act
decisions.reason: The same plea appears in Daniel 9:18. It does not suggest God is deaf, but asks him to treat the matter as his own.

decisions.choice: which he has sent: Sennacherib sent the words through his messengers and his letter
decisions.reason: The words are those of the letter (verses 10-13) and of the Rabshakeh (36:4-20). They were sent to taunt the living God (verse 4).

source.text: אָמְנָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה הֶחֱרִ֜יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת־כָּל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת וְאֶת־אַרְצָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Truly, Yahweh, have laid waste the kings of Assyria all the lands and their land,

en.L: Truly, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the lands and their land,
en.B: It is true, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these lands and their territory,
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, it is true that the kings of Assyria have destroyed all these countries and their lands.

decisions.choice: all the lands and their land: the countries and the territory belonging to them
alternatives: the nations and their land (2 Kings 19:17)
decisions.reason: The phrase is awkward. The parallel 2 Kings 19:17 reads "the nations and their land". Both describe the same devastation, and the sense is not in doubt.

decisions.choice: truly: Hezekiah admits what Sennacherib said is true
decisions.reason: The facts are not in dispute (verses 11-13). The question is what they prove, which the next verse answers.

source.text: וְנָתֹ֥ן אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם בָּאֵ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֣י אִם־מַעֲשֵׂ֧ה יְדֵֽי־אָדָ֛ם עֵ֥ץ וָאֶ֖בֶן וַֽיְאַבְּדֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: and putting their gods in the fire, for not gods [were] they, but [the] work of [the] hands of humankind, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.

en.L: and have put their gods into the fire, for they [were] not gods, but the work of human hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
en.B: and have flung their gods into the fire. Those were never gods, only wood and stone shaped by human hands, so they could destroy them.
en.R: They threw the gods of those nations into the fire and burned them up. But those were not real gods. People had made them out of wood and stone. That is why the Assyrians could destroy them.

decisions.choice: not gods, but the work of human hands: idols have no power of their own
decisions.reason: Isaiah mocks idols as things made by craftsmen (2:8; 40:19-20; 44:9-20). Their defeat proves nothing about the LORD, who made the heavens and the earth (verse 16).

decisions.choice: putting: an infinitive continuing the verb of verse 18
decisions.reason: The form carries on the past action of the previous verse; 2 Kings 19:18 has the finite verb "they have put".

decisions.choice: burned them up; That is why the Assyrians could destroy them
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject and spells out that the gods could be destroyed because they were only objects.

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ מִיָד֑וֹוְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, Yahweh our God, save us from his hand, and may know all [the] kingdoms of the earth that you [are] Yahweh, you alone.

en.L: And now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone."
en.B: So now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, rescue us from his power, so that every kingdom on earth will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Now, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, save us from the king of Assyria. Then all the kingdoms of the earth will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: that all may know that you alone are the LORD: the goal of the rescue is that the nations know God
decisions.reason: Hezekiah asks not only for safety but for God's name to be known (compare 45:6; 1 Kings 18:37). The parallel 2 Kings 19:19 reads "that you, LORD, are God alone".

decisions.choice: from his hand: from his power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control; "his" is Sennacherib.

decisions.choice: from the king of Assyria
decisions.reason: Readable names the one meant by "his".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ הִתְפַּלַּ֣לְתָּ אֵלַ֔י אֶל־סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Isaiah son of Amoz to Hezekiah, saying, Thus says Yahweh God of Israel: that you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,

en.L: And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Because you have prayed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,
en.B: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Because you have prayed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
en.R: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah. He said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: You prayed to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about King Sennacherib of Assyria.

decisions.choice: because you have prayed: the prayer is the occasion of the answer
alternatives: as for what you have prayed
decisions.reason: The clause leads into verse 22. The parallel 2 Kings 19:20 adds "I have heard"; here the answer itself shows that the prayer was heard.

decisions.choice: he sent: Isaiah answers by a message, not in person
decisions.reason: Hezekiah prayed in the temple (verse 14); the answer comes through the prophet, as in verses 5-7. The message runs to verse 35, with a poem against Sennacherib in verses 22-29.

source.text: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן אַחֲרֶ֨יךָ֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הֵנִ֔יעָה בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: this [is] the word that has spoken Yahweh against him: she despises you, she mocks you, [the] virgin daughter of Zion; behind you a head she shakes, [the] daughter of Jerusalem.

en.L: this [is] the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against him: She despises you, she mocks you, the virgin daughter of Zion; behind you she shakes [her] head, the daughter of Jerusalem.
en.B: this is the word {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against him: The virgin, Daughter Zion, looks down on you and laughs at you; Daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at your back.
en.R: So this is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against him: The people of Zion are like a young woman no one has ever conquered. They look down on you and laugh at you. The people of Jerusalem shake their heads at you as you run away.

decisions.choice: the virgin daughter of Zion: Jerusalem pictured as a young woman no enemy has taken
decisions.reason: "Daughter Zion" pictures the city and its people as a young woman (1:8). "Virgin" adds that the invader has not violated her (compare 23:12).

decisions.choice: shakes her head behind you: mockery of an enemy who turns back
decisions.reason: Shaking the head was a gesture of scorn (Psalm 22:8; Lamentations 2:15). "Behind you" pictures Sennacherib retreating while the city mocks him.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion are like a young woman no one has ever conquered; as you run away
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the city and what "behind you" implies.

source.text: אֶת־מִ֤י חֵרַ֨פְתָּ֙ וְגִדַּ֔פְתָּ וְעַל־מִ֖י הֲרִימ֣וֹתָה קּ֑וֹל וַתִּשָּׂ֥א מָר֛וֹם עֵינֶ֖יךָ אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed, and against whom have you raised [your] voice and lifted on high your eyes? Against the Holy One of Israel.

en.L: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed, and against whom have you raised [your] voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!
en.B: Do you know whom you have mocked and reviled? At whom did you shout, at whom did you lift your haughty eyes? At the Holy One of Israel!
en.R: Who is it that you have insulted and spoken against? Who is it that you shouted at and looked at so proudly? It is the Holy One of Israel!

decisions.choice: lifted up your eyes on high: looked with pride and contempt
decisions.reason: Lofty eyes are a picture of arrogance in Isaiah (2:11; 5:15; 10:12).

decisions.choice: the Holy One of Israel: the attack on Jerusalem was an attack on God himself
decisions.reason: Isaiah's favorite name for God comes as the answer to the questions. The king thought he was mocking a small kingdom and its god; he was defying the holy God.

source.text: בְּיַ֣ד עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ חֵרַ֣פְתָּ׀אֲדֹנָי֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרֹ֥ב רִכְבִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י עָלִ֛יתִי מְר֥וֹם הָרִ֖ים יַרְכְּתֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְאֶכְרֹ֞ת קוֹמַ֤ת אֲרָזָיו֙ מִבְחַ֣ר בְּרֹשָׁ֔יו וְאָבוֹא֙ מְר֣וֹם קִצּ֔וֹ יַ֖עַר כַּרְמִלּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: By [the] hand of your servants you have taunted [the] Lord, and you said: with [the] abundance of my chariots I have gone up [the] height of mountains, [the] far reaches of Lebanon; and I will cut down [the] tallness of its cedars, [the] choicest of its junipers; and I will come [to the] height of its end, [the] forest of its garden land.

en.L: By the hand of your servants you have taunted the Lord, and you said, 'With the multitude of my chariots I have gone up [to] the height of the mountains, [to] the far reaches of Lebanon, and I will cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest junipers, and I will come [to] its farthest height, the forest of its garden land.
en.B: Through your servants you have mocked the Lord. You said, 'With chariots past counting I have climbed the mountain heights, the far ridges of Lebanon. I will fell its loftiest cedars and its finest junipers. I will reach its farthest summit and its lush forest.
en.R: You sent your officials to insult the Lord. You said, 'I have many chariots. With them I have climbed the highest mountains, even the farthest mountains of Lebanon. I will cut down its tallest cedar trees and its best juniper trees. I will go to its highest peaks and its thickest forests.

decisions.choice: I have gone up ... I will cut down ... I will come: boasts of what he has done and what he will do
alternatives: all past: I cut down ... I reached
decisions.reason: The first verb is a past form; the next two are forms usually read as future. The king boasts of conquests behind him and promises more. They can also be read as past ("I cut down ... I came").

decisions.choice: felling the cedars of Lebanon: a royal boast of power over the land
decisions.reason: Assyrian kings recorded in their inscriptions that they crossed mountains with their chariots and cut cedars in Lebanon for their buildings. Isaiah uses the same picture to show Assyria's pride brought down (10:33-34; 14:8).

decisions.choice: your servants ... the Lord
decisions.reason: The parallel 2 Kings 19:23 reads "your messengers". Both mean the envoys who spoke for the king (36:4-20).

source.text: אֲנִ֥י קַ֖רְתִּי וְשָׁתִ֣יתִי מָ֑יִם וְאַחְרִב֙ בְּכַף־פְּעָמַ֔י כֹּ֖ל יְאֹרֵ֥י מָצֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: I have dug and I have drunk water, and I will dry up with [the] sole of my feet all [the] streams of Egypt.

en.L: I have dug and drunk water, and I will dry up with the sole of my feet all the streams of Egypt.'
en.B: I have dug wells and drunk their water, and under the tread of my feet every stream of Egypt will run dry.'
en.R: I have dug wells and drunk water from them. I will march through Egypt and dry up all its streams under my feet.'

decisions.choice: Egypt: a poetic name for the land
decisions.reason: The same word is used for Egypt in 19:6. Some take it as "siege" or "fortified places".

decisions.choice: water
decisions.reason: The parallel 2 Kings 19:24 reads "foreign water", meaning he drank in lands he invaded. The sense here is the same: wherever he goes he can find water for his army.

decisions.choice: I will dry up the streams: the king claims a power that belongs to God
decisions.reason: Drying up rivers is what God does (11:15; 19:5-6; 50:2). God answers the boast in the next verse.

decisions.choice: wells
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was dug.

source.text: הֲלֽוֹא־שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵאתִ֔יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לְהַשְׁא֛וֹת גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Have you not heard? From afar it I made, from days of old and I formed it; now I have brought it, and you are to lay waste [into] heaps ruined cities fortified.

en.L: Have you not heard? From long ago I did it; from days of old I formed it. Now I have brought it about, and you are [here] to lay waste fortified cities [into] ruined heaps.
en.B: Have you not heard? I did this long ago; in days of old I shaped it. Now I have made it happen, so that you turn walled cities into heaps of rubble.
en.R: Have you not heard? I planned this long ago. I decided it in days long past. Now I have made it happen. I let you turn strong, walled cities into piles of ruins.

decisions.choice: I made it, I formed it, I have brought it: Assyria's conquests were God's plan
decisions.reason: God answers the boast: the king did nothing on his own. God formed the plan long ago, like a potter shaping a pot (22:11), and Assyria was only his tool (10:5-15).

decisions.choice: and you are to lay waste: you exist for this purpose
decisions.reason: The verb with an infinitive describes the role God gave the king: to turn cities into ruins.

decisions.choice: I let you
decisions.reason: Readable expresses that the king's role was given to him by God.

source.text: וְיֹֽשְׁבֵיהֶן֙ קִצְרֵי־יָ֔ד חַ֖תּוּ וָבֹ֑שׁוּ הָי֞וּ עֵ֤שֶׂב שָׂדֶה֙ וִ֣ירַק דֶּ֔שֶׁא חֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֔וֹת וּשְׁדֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י קָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And their inhabitants [were] short of hand; they were dismayed and ashamed; they were plants of [the] field and green of fresh grass, grass of roofs, and a field before standing grain.

en.L: And their inhabitants [were] short of hand; they were dismayed and put to shame; they were [like] plants of the field and green herbs, grass of the roofs, and a field before standing grain.
en.B: Their people were powerless, terrified and put to shame. They were like the plants of the open field and fresh green herbs, like grass on a rooftop, like a field of young shoots before the grain stands tall.
en.R: That is why the people of those cities were weak. They were afraid and ashamed. They were like plants and grass in a field. They were like grass growing on a flat roof, which dries up quickly. They were like a field of young grain that withers before it grows tall.

decisions.choice: short of hand: without power
decisions.reason: A short hand cannot reach or act (50:2; 59:1). The cities' people had no strength to resist.

decisions.choice: a field before standing grain: young shoots that have not grown up and wither easily
alternatives: scorched before it is grown (2 Kings 19:26)
decisions.reason: The phrase is difficult. The parallel 2 Kings 19:26 reads "scorched before it is grown", and the Great Isaiah Scroll appears to read "scorched before the east wind". All the readings picture young growth that is easily destroyed.

decisions.choice: grass of the roofs: grass sprouting in the thin soil of flat roofs
decisions.reason: Such grass withers before it grows (Psalm 129:6).

decisions.choice: That is why; which dries up quickly; that withers
decisions.reason: Readable states the link with verse 26 and the point of the comparisons.

source.text: וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ וְצֵאתְךָ֥ וּבוֹאֲךָ֖ יָדָ֑עְתִּי וְאֵ֖ת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ֥ אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And your sitting down and your going out and your coming in I know, and your raging against me.

en.L: And your sitting down and your going out and your coming in I know, and your raging against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: I know where you sit, when you go out and when you come in, and how you storm against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I know everything you do. I know when you rest and when you come and go. And I know how angry you are with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: your sitting, your going out, your coming in: everything you do
decisions.reason: The pairs sum up all of a person's life and actions (Deuteronomy 28:6; Psalm 121:8; 139:2). Nothing the king does is hidden from God.

decisions.choice: raging: a stirred-up, violent anger
decisions.reason: The verb means to tremble or be agitated, here with fury against God.

decisions.choice: I know everything you do
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense of the pairs first.

source.text: יַ֚עַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ֣ אֵלַ֔י וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ֖ עָלָ֣ה בְאָזְנָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁ֣יבֹתִ֔יךָ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אתָ בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Because your raging against me and your arrogance has come up into my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.

en.L: Because of your raging against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and your arrogance has come up into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears, I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hook in your nose and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.
en.B: Since you rage against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and your arrogance has come up to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears, I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hook in your nose and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bit between your lips, and I will lead you back along the same road by which you came.
en.R: You have been angry with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I have heard your proud words. So I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hook in your nose and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} bit in your mouth, as people do to lead an animal. I will force you to go back home by the same road you came on.

decisions.choice: a hook in the nose, a bridle in the lips: led away like a beast or a captive
decisions.reason: Animals were led by rings through the nose (Ezekiel 19:4; 29:4), and Assyrian kings showed captive rulers led by cords fastened to their lips. God will treat the conqueror as he treated others.

decisions.choice: your arrogance: proud, careless confidence
decisions.reason: The word describes a person at ease who thinks nothing can touch him (32:9).

decisions.choice: turn you back by the way you came: fulfilled when he goes home
decisions.reason: The promise is repeated in verse 34 and fulfilled in verse 37.

decisions.choice: as people do to lead an animal; back home
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture and where the road leads (verse 37).

source.text: וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת אָכ֤וֹל הַשָּׁנָה֙ סָפִ֔יחַ וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית שָׁחִ֑יס וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗ית זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים וְאִכְל֥וּ פִרְיָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] for you the sign: eating this year aftergrowth, and in the year the second self-sown grain, and in the year the third sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

en.L: And this [is] the sign for you: eating this year what grows by itself, and in the second year what springs up from that, and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
en.B: Here is the sign for you: this year you will live on grain that sprang up untended, and next year on whatever comes up after it; but in the third year, sow and harvest, plant vineyards and eat what they bear.
en.R: Hezekiah, this will be a sign for you. This year you will eat grain that grows wild. Next year you will eat grain that comes up from that. But in the third year you will plant your crops and harvest them. You will plant vineyards and eat their grapes.

decisions.choice: what grows by itself: grain sprouting from seed spilled at the last harvest
decisions.reason: With the Assyrian army in the land, no crops could be sown. The words are those used for the sabbatical year (Leviticus 25:5, 11). The people will live on what comes up without sowing until normal farming returns.

decisions.choice: the sign for you: addressed to Hezekiah, with commands to the people
decisions.reason: "You" is singular, but "sow", "reap" and "plant" are plural. The sign is confirmed after the event, as in Exodus 3:12: the people will live to farm in peace again.

decisions.choice: and eat: the reading of the traditional reading notes
decisions.reason: The written text has the infinitive "and eating"; the margin reads the plural command "and eat". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Hezekiah
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed; Isaiah turns from Sennacherib to the king.

source.text: וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית־יְהוּדָ֛ה הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ לְמָ֑טָּה וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י לְמָֽעְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will add the escaped of the house of Judah that remains [to take] root downward and will produce fruit upward.

en.L: And the escaped of the house of Judah that remains will again [take] root downward and bear fruit upward.
en.B: Those of the house of Judah who escape and are left will once more put down roots below and bear fruit above.
en.R: Once again the people of Judah who are left will be like a plant. They will send their roots down deep and grow fruit up high.

decisions.choice: the escaped that remains: the survivors of Judah
decisions.reason: The same words describe those who survive God's judgment in 4:2 and 10:20.

decisions.choice: root below and fruit above: new life and prosperity
decisions.reason: A plant rooted deep and bearing fruit is a picture of a people restored (27:6; compare the reverse in Amos 2:9).

decisions.choice: will be like a plant
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison explicit.

source.text: כִּ֤י מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ תֵּצֵ֣א שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה מֵהַ֣ר צִיּ֑וֹן קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־זֹּֽאת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For from Jerusalem will go out a remnant, and an escaped [band] from [the] mountain of Zion. The zeal of Yahweh of hosts will do this.

en.L: For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and an escaped band from Mount Zion. The zeal of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will do this.
en.B: For a remnant will go out from Jerusalem, and from Mount Zion those who have escaped. The burning zeal of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will make this happen.
en.R: A group of survivors will come out of Jerusalem, out of Mount Zion. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies has set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart on doing this, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do it.

decisions.choice: will go out: the survivors leave the city freely once the siege is over
decisions.reason: The people shut up in Jerusalem will go out again to live and farm (verses 30-31).

decisions.choice: the zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this: the same words as 9:6
decisions.reason: God's burning commitment to his people guarantees the promise. In the parallel 2 Kings 19:31 the written text lacks "of hosts", which the margin supplies.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לֹ֤א יָבוֹא֙ אֶל־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹֽא־יוֹרֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם חֵ֑ץ וְלֹֽא־יְקַדְּמֶ֣נָּה מָגֵ֔ן וְלֹֽא־יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ עֳלֶ֖יהָסֹלְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh concerning [the] king of Assyria: not he will come into the city this, and not he will shoot there an arrow, and not he will come before it [with a] shield, and not he will pour out against it a siege mound.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning the king of Assyria: He will not come into this city, and he will not shoot an arrow there, and he will not come before it [with] a shield, and he will not pour out a siege mound against it.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this about the king of Assyria: He will never set foot in this city. He will not fire a single arrow into it, nor face it with a shield, nor pile up an earthen ramp against its walls.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about the king of Assyria: He will not come into this city. He will not shoot even one arrow here. His soldiers will not march up to it with shields. They will not build a ramp of dirt against its walls.

decisions.choice: pour out a siege mound: heap up an earthen ramp against the wall
decisions.reason: Attackers built ramps of earth and stone to bring battering rams up to a city's walls. The Assyrian siege ramp at Lachish has been excavated.

decisions.choice: he will not come into this city: a promise of complete protection
decisions.reason: Not only will the city not fall; the siege will not even begin. Sennacherib's own annals say he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem, but they do not claim that he took the city.

decisions.choice: His soldiers ... They
decisions.reason: Readable names the army that would carry the shields and build the ramp; the king acts through it.

source.text: בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖א בָּ֣הּ יָשׁ֑וּב וְאֶל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: By the way that he came, by it he will return, and into the city this not he will come, declares Yahweh.

en.L: By the way by which he came, by it he will return, and into this city he will not come, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The road that brought him here will take him back again. This city he will not enter, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He will go back home the same way he came. He will not come into this city, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: by the way he came he will return: repeats verse 29
decisions.reason: The promise to the king of Assyria matches the end of the poem (verse 29) and comes true in verse 37.

source.text: וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will defend over the city this to save it, for my sake and for the sake of David my servant.

en.L: And I will defend this city, to save it, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake and for the sake of David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant."
en.B: I will shield this city and rescue it, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own sake and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David's sake."
en.R: I will protect this city and save it. I will do this for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own honor, and because of the promise I made to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David."

decisions.choice: defend: cover over and shield
decisions.reason: The verb pictures God spreading his protection over the city (31:5; 38:6).

decisions.choice: for my sake and for David's sake: God acts for his own name and his promise to David
decisions.reason: God saves to uphold his honor before the nations (verse 20; 43:25; 48:11) and to keep his promise that David's line would rule in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 7:16; 1 Kings 11:13).

decisions.choice: for my own honor; because of the promise I made to my servant David
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "for my sake" and "for David's sake" mean.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א׀מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּכֶּה֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה אַשּׁ֔וּר מֵאָ֛ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֥ה כֻלָּ֖ם פְּגָרִ֥ים מֵתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] angel of Yahweh and struck down in [the] camp of Assyria a hundred and eighty-five thousand; and they rose early in the morning, and look, all of them [were] corpses, dead.

en.L: And the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went out and struck down in the camp of Assyria 185,000; and they rose early in the morning, and look, all of them [were] dead bodies.
en.B: Then the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went out and struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp. At dawn, when people got up, they found them all lying dead.
en.R: Then the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went out to the camp of the Assyrian army and killed 185,000 soldiers. Early the next morning, when people woke up, they saw that all of those soldiers were dead.

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD: God's messenger acting with his power
decisions.reason: The angel of the LORD carries out God's judgment, as on Egypt's firstborn (Exodus 12:23) and on Israel in David's time (2 Samuel 24:16). The text does not say how the soldiers died.

decisions.choice: they rose early: people, not named
decisions.reason: The subject is not the dead soldiers but those who rose in the morning, whether survivors in the camp or people of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the end of the campaign: Assyria's records do not report the capture of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Sennacherib's annals boast that he shut Hezekiah in Jerusalem "like a bird in a cage" and received heavy tribute, but tell of no capture. The Greek historian Herodotus (Histories 2.141) records an Egyptian story of a disaster that struck Sennacherib's army in one night.

decisions.choice: men (B); soldiers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the 185,000 were.

source.text: וַיִּסַּ֣ע וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖שָׁב סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּנִֽינְוֵֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out and went and returned Sennacherib king of Assyria, and he stayed in Nineveh.

en.L: And Sennacherib king of Assyria set out and went and returned, and he stayed in Nineveh.
en.B: So Sennacherib king of Assyria struck camp and went away. He returned home and stayed in Nineveh.
en.R: So King Sennacherib of Assyria packed up his camp and left. He went back to Nineveh, his capital city, and lived there.

decisions.choice: Nineveh: the capital of Assyria under Sennacherib
decisions.reason: Sennacherib rebuilt Nineveh, on the Tigris River, as his royal city.

decisions.choice: returned: God's word comes true
decisions.reason: The king goes home as God said he would (verses 7, 29, 34).

decisions.choice: his capital city
decisions.reason: Readable explains what Nineveh was.

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית׀נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר בָּנָיו֙ הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, he [was] bowing down [in the] house of Nisroch his god, and Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword, and they escaped [to the] land of Ararat. And became king Esarhaddon his son in his place.

en.L: And it was, [as] he [was] bowing down [in] the house of Nisroch his god, [that] Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword, and they escaped [to] the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.
en.B: While he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his own sons, cut him down with the sword and fled to the land of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.
en.R: Later, Sennacherib was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch. While he was there, two of his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with a sword. Then they ran away to the land of Ararat, in the mountains to the north. Another son, Esarhaddon, became the next king of Assyria.

decisions.choice: his death: Sennacherib was murdered in 681 BC, about twenty years after the campaign
decisions.reason: The Babylonian Chronicle records that Sennacherib was killed by his son in a revolt, and that Esarhaddon followed him as king. This fulfills the word of verse 7: he fell by the sword in his own land.

decisions.choice: Nisroch: an Assyrian god not otherwise known by this name
decisions.reason: The god's identity is uncertain; the name may be a form of the name of a known Assyrian god.

decisions.choice: the land of Ararat: Urartu, a kingdom in the mountains north of Assyria
decisions.reason: The same name is used for the mountains where the ark came to rest (Genesis 8:4). Urartu was Assyria's rival, a refuge beyond its reach.

decisions.choice: Later; in the mountains to the north
decisions.reason: Readable marks that the murder came years after the campaign (see m1) and locates Ararat.
